Summary: The paper presents ReAgent, a four-stage Detect–Fix–Retrain–Gate pipeline aimed at mitigating structural tool-calling hallucinations (unavailable tools, invalid or placeholder arguments, and repetitive loops) in an open-weight agent (Aya Expanse 32B) evaluated on τ²-bench (retail, airline, and telecom). ReAgent combines a deterministic rule-based Tool/Arg/Loop failure classifier, oracle-verified trajectory distillation from an open-weight teacher (GLM-5.3-Flash), agent-turn-masked QLoRA fine-tuning, and a pre-registered four-check development deployment gate (DevGate). On the 100-task held-out τ²-bench test split, the fine-tuned adapter (Arm B / SFT v2) reduces Tool/Arg hallucination conversations from 95.0% to 10.0% and improves task success from 14.5% to 51.5%, whereas an anti-hallucination prompt achieves 13.0%. The authors also compare turn-level versus trajectory-level healing cycles, conduct SFT data/step ablations, report negative results for three single-turn post-SFT GRPO variants that suffer from dialogue collapse or structural reward hacking, and analyze residual non-structural policy errors.
Strengths: Disciplined experimental protocol and statistical rigor: strict train/val/dev/test split isolation enforced programmatically (`assert_not_test()`), independent outcome-oracle verification on the test split (0/600 disagreements), pre-registered DevGate and adoption thresholds, paired task-level bootstrap confidence intervals, Wilson intervals, and Holm-corrected exact McNemar tests.

Candid and transparent reporting of negative results and failure modes, including the failure of anti-hallucination prompting, SFT v1's airline regression, fixed-step telecom dilution in SFT v3/v4, the non-firing live `no_progress` monitor, context overflows, and three failing post-SFT GRPO variants.

Actionable qualitative error analyses: pinpointing why untuned Aya calls customer-only telecom tools (function-call syntax in `tech_support_manual.md`), documenting how structural RL rewards (GRPO Arm H) halve loops while inducing syntactically valid but unrequested write actions (e.g., extra airline cancellations), and demonstrating that 37/55 post-healing failures contain zero structural hallucinations.

Practical cost-effectiveness analysis showing that ~$11 of verified teacher trajectories and under 30 minutes of single-H100 QLoRA training substantially recover a weak 32B model, alongside a clear demonstration of why multi-metric deployment gates are necessary.
Weaknesses: Disconnect between the 'closed-loop self-healing' framing and the actual working mechanism: the promoted model (Arm B / SFT v2) is effectively single-round offline oracle-verified teacher–student trajectory distillation supplemented by manual, dev-informed domain rebalancing (34 extra airline trajectories added after SFT v1 failed DevGate). In trajectory mode, the Tool/Arg/Loop classifier does not guide synthesis (the teacher simply solves failed tasks from `s0`), Cycle 2 reuses SFT v2's dev-informed pool rather than operating autonomously, and every targeted or iterative mechanism (Cycle 1 turn-level rewrites, SFT v4 on-policy fixing, live monitoring, GRPO) fails to improve over SFT v2.

Severely confounded fix-granularity comparison (Cycle 1 vs. Cycle 2, Section 4.4): the claimed effect of turn-level versus trajectory-level fixing is not experimentally isolated because the two cycles simultaneously vary task pool size (30 vs. 112 tasks), deduplication (capped at 2 per lesson yielding 16 turns vs. 136 full conversations with extra airline passes), target token volume (938 tokens vs. full multi-turn trajectories), optimizer steps/batch size (16 vs. 68 steps), and dev-informed domain balancing.

Missing strong inference-time baselines and test-set serving confounds: (a) comparing fine-tuning only against a brief zero-shot anti-hallucination prompt (Arm C) is insufficient to claim structural hallucination is purely a data problem—obvious zero-training baselines such as schema/grammar-constrained decoding (natively supported in vLLM), few-shot teacher examples, or using the authors' own deterministic classifier as a pre-execution runtime guardrail with structured feedback are omitted; (b) on the held-out Test split, Arm B runs on local vLLM (32K context) while Arms A and C run on Cohere's hosted API (128K context), omitting the self-hosted untuned control (Arm P) and teacher (GLM-5.3-Flash) from Test and confounding accuracy and latency.

Narrow scope, weak student motivation, and oracle dependency: experiments cover only one English benchmark (τ²-bench) and one unusually weak base model (Aya Expanse 32B, 14.5% baseline), even though similarly sized or smaller open-weight models in the authors' own bake-off (e.g., Qwen3.8 27B, Gemma 4 31B, GLM-5.3-Flash) outperform healed Aya out of the box. Furthermore, heavy reliance on a ground-truth environment database oracle (`V(τ)`) and simulated user to replay episodes from `s0` limits applicability to genuine post-deployment settings.

Methodological and validation gaps: the 30-task validation split is non-randomly constructed ('15 tasks solved by base Aya and 15 without a teacher fix'), complicating interpretation of validation scores; classifier precision is spot-checked on only 30 telecom failures (with no retail/airline check and unmeasured recall); SFT v4 (DAgger-style on-policy fixing) was compromised by an accounting bug and mid-run API credit exhaustion; and GRPO conclusions are overgeneralized from single-turn static-prefix surrogate rewards rather than multi-turn outcome-reward RL.

Scholarly and presentation issues: the bibliography has only 9 entries and omits citations for core foundations including τ²-bench, QLoRA, GRPO, and DAgger; key tools (`AuditKIT`, `AgentTune`) are left undefined/uncited; the classifier is inconsistently described as 10 sub-kinds while listing 12 kinds (2 TOOL + 6 ARG + 4 LOOP); and Tables 4 and 8 suffer from margin clipping and stray characters.
Questions: In `--fix-mode trajectory`, what substantive role does the deterministic Tool/Arg/Loop classifier play in the Fix and Retrain stages beyond logging and DevGate Check 3, given that failures are selected by `V(τ)=0` and the teacher solves tasks from `s0` filtered by `V(τ_teach)=1`?
If Cycle 2 is run truly autonomously from scratch without reusing SFT v2's manually dev-informed airline oversampling, does it pass DevGate or fail Check 4 like SFT v1?

What are the results of a controlled fix-granularity ablation that matches the training task pool (all 112 tasks), removes the aggressive 2-per-lesson deduplication cap, and controls for optimizer steps and target token budget between turn-level rewrites and full-trajectory distillation?

How much of the 14.5% → 51.5% gain can be achieved without weight updates by using your deterministic Tool/Arg/Loop classifier as a pre-execution runtime interceptor returning actionable error feedback, or via vLLM schema/grammar-constrained decoding and few-shot prompting?

Can you evaluate the self-hosted untuned control (Arm P) and the teacher (GLM-5.3-Flash) on the 100-task held-out Test split to eliminate the Cohere-API vs. vLLM serving confound and establish the distillation recovery ratio?

Why was Aya Expanse 32B chosen as the sole student when similar or smaller open-weight models already outperform healed Aya zero-shot, and does ReAgent yield meaningful improvements when applied to a stronger open-weight base agent?
Why was the 30-task validation split constructed specifically from 15 tasks solved by base Aya and 15 without a teacher fix, and can you clearly define and cite AuditKIT and AgentTune?
Limitations: Evaluation is restricted to a single English customer-service benchmark (τ²-bench) and a single weak base student model (Aya Expanse 32B), leaving cross-model, cross-benchmark, and multilingual generalization untested.

Strong dependence on a much more capable teacher model, a simulated user, and a ground-truth environment outcome oracle (`V(τ)`), which are generally unavailable in live post-deployment production environments.
No evaluation of catastrophic forgetting or general-capability retention outside the three narrow customer-service schemas after QLoRA adaptation.
Unmeasured classifier recall and very limited precision validation (30 telecom conversations only), leaving diagnostic reliability across retail and airline domains unquantified.

Operational safety risks in write-enabled production environments: as illustrated by GRPO Arm H, optimizing structural compliance does not prevent harmful unauthorized database mutations without explicit transactional confirmation guards.
